mcqs.question: Consider the two diagrams below. Diagram I shows three lines that intersect pairwise at three different points forming a small triangle. Diagram II shows three lines where all three meet at a single point. Which statement correctly compares the two configurations?

options.A: Both diagrams have the same number of intersection points.
options.B: Diagram I has three intersection points, while Diagram II has only one.
options.C: Diagram I has one intersection point, while Diagram II has three.
options.D: Both diagrams have no intersection points.

mcqs.answer: Diagram I has three intersection points, while Diagram II has only one.
mcqs.explanation: In Diagram I each pair of lines meets at a different point, giving three distinct intersection points. In Diagram II all three lines are concurrent, meeting at one common point. Therefore option B correctly compares the configurations.

mcqs.question: In a figure, three straight lines L1, L2, and L3 intersect such that L1 meets L2 at point P, L2 meets L3 at point Q, and L1 meets L3 at point R. How many distinct intersection points are there in total?
mcqs.explanation: Each pair of lines meets at a different point (P, Q, R). No two pairs share the same point, so there are three distinct intersection points. Options A, B, and D are therefore incorrect.

mcqs.question: When two of the three lines intersect, they form vertical angles. Which pair of angles are vertical angles?

options.A: Angles at the same side of the intersecting lines
options.B: Angles opposite each other across the intersection point

mcqs.answer: Angles opposite each other across the intersection point
mcqs.explanation: Vertical angles are the non‑adjacent angles that lie opposite each other when two lines cross. They are equal in measure. Option B describes this correctly; the other options describe adjacent or supplementary relationships.

mcqs.question: Which description best matches a configuration where three lines intersect but no two are parallel and they do not all meet at a single point?

options.B: All three lines intersect at one common point
options.C: Each pair of lines meets at a different point

mcqs.answer: Each pair of lines meets at a different point
mcqs.explanation: When no two lines are parallel and they are not concurrent, each pair intersects at its own point, giving three distinct intersection points. Options A, B, and D describe different situations.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes between a "triangle formed by three intersecting lines" and "three concurrent lines"?

options.A: A triangle has three intersection points, while concurrent lines have only one common point
options.B: Both have exactly one intersection point
options.D: Concurrent lines form a closed shape

mcqs.answer: A triangle has three intersection points, while concurrent lines have only one common point
mcqs.explanation: Three lines that intersect pairwise create three distinct points, the vertices of a triangle. If the three lines are concurrent, they all meet at a single point. Hence option A correctly distinguishes the two configurations.

mcqs.question: Line a, line b, and line c are drawn on a board. a and b intersect at point X, b and c intersect at point Y. What is the intersection point of lines a and c?
mcqs.explanation: The problem states that each pair of lines meets at a distinct point. Since X is a∩b and Y is b∩c, the remaining pair a∩c must be a third point, labelled Z. Therefore option C is correct.

mcqs.question: In a diagram, line AB meets line CD at point O forming an angle of 40°. Line EF also passes through O making an angle of 70° with AB on the same side. What is the measure of the smallest angle formed between CD and EF?
mcqs.explanation: Angle between CD and AB is 40°. Angle between AB and EF is 70°. The angle between CD and EF equals the difference: 70° − 40° = 30°, which is the smallest angle. Options B, C, and D do not match this calculation.

mcqs.question: Three roads A, B, and C intersect in a town. Road A crosses Road B at point P, Road B crosses Road C at point Q, and Road A crosses Road C at point R. Which term best describes this arrangement?
mcqs.explanation: Each pair of roads meets at a different point, forming three vertices P, Q, and R that outline a triangle. Hence the arrangement is a triangular road network. The other options describe different configurations.
